idiom_name: golang.org/x/time/rate NewLimiter (token bucket) with Allow / Reserve / Wait
implementation_notes: The canonical Go realization is golang.org/x/time/rate, the official quasi-standard library: NewLimiter(r, b) creates a token bucket of size b refilled at r tokens per second, and the type is documented as safe for simultaneous use by multiple goroutines. The three methods encode the three policies - Allow drops the event, Reserve returns a Reservation whose Delay the caller honours or cancels, and Wait blocks until a token is available, the context is cancelled or its deadline passes. In HTTP handlers Allow plus 429 and Retry-After is the customary form; workers that must not lose work call WaitN or Wait(ctx) so the call is paced instead of refused.
pitfalls: The zero-value Limiter rejects everything; use NewLimiter (or set Limit/Burst) rather than relying on the zero value.
Wait returns an error when n exceeds the burst or the context deadline expires; ignoring it turns the limiter into a silent fail-open.
A per-key limiter map grows without bound unless idle entries are evicted; keys need bounded cardinality or a TTL sweep.
The limiter is per process: N replicas admit N times the configured rate against a shared dependency.
